subject: FastShop inference pathing: hosted or dedicated?
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@fastshop.com>, Tony Reed <tony@fastshop.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 14:08:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + clarifying asks from today's scout call

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation. Short recap and a few quick asks so we can recommend the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private).

What I captured from the call
- Workload: conversational assistant for checkout + post-purchase support.
- Latency objective: p95 under 150ms perceived by API consumer; some UI components can accept up to 300ms.
- Traffic signal: steady-state ~600–900 QPS, short peaks up to ~2.5k for ~5–15 minutes during promos.
- Model: planning to use a 13B variant (few-shot prompts, ~1k token context).
- Data sensitivity: customer identifiers + order metadata (PII); must remain within US regions.
- Timeline: procurement in Jan, pilot in Feb.

Clarifying asks (will let us size a recommended path):
1) Can you send a 24–72h traffic export with 1-min granularity (we need burst shape, not just daily QPS).
2) Confirm typical request token lengths (prompt+expected response) so we can estimate compute.
3) Any hard SLA / contractual latency target (e.g., p95 <= 100ms) vs internal goal?
4) Is encryption-at-rest + KMS integration required for pilot or only production?

What we'll propose once we have the data
- Hosted API option: aggressive caching + autoscaling; lower ops but may have slightly wider latency variance during extreme bursts; good for faster time-to-value.
- Dedicated option: reserved GPU pool sized for your steady state with headroom for short bursts; predictable p95 latency and isolation; better for strict latency SLOs.
- Private/VPC: recommended only if procurement or compliance requires customer-controlled network/KMS.

Attachments: call recording + small template for traffic export — please attach when you have a moment.

Next step: Elena/Tony — if you can share the traffic snapshot and token-size samples today or Monday we can turn around a short one-pager with recommended config + rough cost delta.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Steady traffic: typically 700–850 QPS during business hours (US), with marketing-driven flashes up to 2.5k for 5–12 minutes. Spikes are very bursty (roughly exponential tail).
- Typical tokens: prompt ~220 tokens, expected response ~300 tokens (avg ~520 total).

- Region: US only for now; latency-sensitive users are east and central US.

Forwarding Elena's response and the attachments — see traffic CSV. Need an internal quick recommendation (one-paragraph) we can send back to FastShop by EOD: Hosted pilot vs Dedicated pilot and a sketch of expected p95 latency and approximate monthly cost range for the described profile.

Key inputs from Elena: steady 700–850 QPS, burst to 2.5k (5–12m), avg request ~520 tokens, east/central US sensitivity, internal goal p95 <= 150ms (procurement may push 120ms). Pilot allowed to use Redwood-managed KMS.

My thinking: two candidate paths to propose to reduce friction for procurement
- Option A (Fastest TTV): Hosted API with aggressive prefix caching + request caching, dedicated autoscaling policy for promo windows, and profile tuning (quantized 13B). Expected p95 ~140–220ms depending on burst shape; lower cost up-front, riskier under multi-region simultaneous promos.
- Option B (Predictable SLOs): Reserved Dedicated pool sized for sustained 850 QPS (with 20% headroom) + pre-warmed burst capacity. Expected p95 ~80–140ms for the 13B quantized profile; higher committed cost but better predictability.

Can you 1) validate the latency ranges above quickly using the traffic CSV, and 2) propose a minimal Dedicated config (GPU types / count) and a 30-day pilot plan (what we need from FastShop vs what Redwood will deliver)?

Thanks — I'm proposing we keep this to a 1-pager and a pilot statement of work to keep procurement moving.

— Jordan

Thanks for the forward — quick notes based on the CSV and the token samples. TL;DR: recommend Dedicated reserved capacity for pilot given FastShop's burstiness and their p95 target.

Reasoning / configuration suggestion
- Model: 13B quantized (int8-ish profile) — good balance of quality/cost.
- Baseline sizing: target sustained 900 QPS -> roughly 4x H100-equivalent workers (estimate) with continuous batching and KV caching for common prefixes. That should give p95 ~85–130ms with current token profile.
- Burst handling: configure burst pool of additional 2 workers that can spin up with pre-warm hooks (we can hold warm instances for predictable promo windows).
- Fallback: provide a Hosted fallback policy for cross-region failover; cost modeled separately.

Pilot plan (30 days, low-risk)
1) Redwood to provision Dedicated sandbox in US region with KMS-integrated logging + access for FastShop devs.
2) FastShop to grant traffic routing to sandbox and share anonymized production traces for the first 72h.
3) Joint perf run: two-day load run to validate p95 under promos; adjustments day 3.
4) Deliverables: perf report, cost estimate for committed capacity, runbook for failover to Hosted.

Attachments: redwood-capacity-proposal-13B.pdf (sketch of costs + GPU config).

I'll draft the 1-pager and the pilot SOW — Jordan, if you can confirm procurement timelines I'll lace in billing terms for a 3-month commit option (usually preferred for price).
